title: Tech Note: Web Serving the 4D Ajax Framework on 4D Client
author: Jason Zajdel
featured_technology: Web server deployment on client machine

historical_commentary.text: This note details the deployment architecture for hosting 4DAF on a 4D Client machine as an intermediary web server between external users and a protected 4D Server database. The approach offered resource and security advantages by isolating the main database server while allowing web-based access through a client-machine publisher. This deployment pattern became obsolete as 4D's web architecture evolved, particularly with the introduction of Project Mode (v17, 2018) and Qodly, which removed the need for separate client-publisher machines and integrated web publishing directly into the server.
related_updates: 4D Web 2.0 Pack (4DAF) itself was discontinued, replaced by 4D Web Components and Qodly
Modern 4D web publishing is now integral to 4D Server with built-in RESTful API support and mobile/web frameworks
The client-as-publisher pattern is no longer a recommended or supported deployment model
